chunks: Ibn Abī Naṣr narrated from Dāwūd ibn Sirḥān, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام:
Concerning a man who carried goods on his head, then struck a person so that he died, or something was broken because of it: then he is liable.

key_terms.رَأْسِهِ: his head, indicating the manner of carrying
key_terms.ضَامِنٌ: legally liable or responsible for compensation
key_terms.فَأَصَابَ: then he struck or affected, causing harm
key_terms.ٱنْكَسَرَ: was broken, referring to damaged property or object

ai.seo_question: Is a person liable if something he carries causes death or property damage?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on liability for harm caused while carrying goods. If a person causes death or property damage in this way, he is held responsible for the resulting harm.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3932 - Ibn Abi Nasr narrated from Dawood bin Sirhan, from Abu Abdillah (as):
"If a man carries goods on his head and accidentally strikes someone, causing their death or breaking something, then he is liable."
